PullRequest.Title: customizations: allow uninstalling MCP servers from shared configuration files
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #344539

## Context

In **Customizations > MCP Servers**, each row has a **More actions** (…) menu. I checked every kind of row in Code OSS:

| Row source | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| User `mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, workspace root `.mcp.json` | Uninstall | Unchanged |
| Copilot CLI `mcp-config.json` (now the recommended user configuration) | **No way to remove** | **Uninstall** removes it from the file after a confirmation |
| Claude Desktop, Cursor or Windsurf configuration file | **No way to remove** | **Uninstall** explains that VS Code can't edit that file and offers **Show Configuration** |
| Extension (other than Copilot) | **No way to remove** | **Uninstall** explains that the extension provides it and offers **Show Extension** |
| Plugin | Uninstall Plugin | Unchanged |
| Connector | Disconnect | Unchanged |
| Copilot's own built-in servers | Enable/disable only | Unchanged (they can only be disabled) |

## Changes

- `IEditableMcpServerConfiguration` (used for the shared `.mcp.json` and Copilot CLI `mcp-config.json` files the detail form already edits) gains `remove()`, which uses the existing `IMcpResourceScannerService.removeMcpServers` for that file format.
- Built-in rows with a configuration file or non-Copilot extension source get **Uninstall** as the last menu group. When run, it checks whether VS Code can edit the source file:
  - If it can, it confirms (the file is shared with other MCP clients such as the Copilot CLI) and removes the entry. The row then disappears through the existing file watcher.
  - If it can't, it explains where the server must be removed and offers to open that source.
- **Show Output** is now inserted above Uninstall rather than after it, so the destructive action stays last.

## Not covered

- Servers that only the agent host reports, with no matching local configuration, still offer no removal.
- The server detail page still has no Uninstall button; removal is in the row menu.
- A Copilot CLI configuration on a remote machine gets the explanation rather than removal, because only the local file is resolved as editable.

## Validation

- Manually tested in Code OSS with servers in user `mcp.json`, `.vscode/mcp.json`, root `.mcp.json`, `COPILOT_HOME/mcp-config.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json`. Uninstalling the Copilot CLI server removed it from the file and the list.
- `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/mcpListWidget.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/embeddedMcpServerDetail.test.ts`: passed (168 tests)
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>`: passed

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the MCP Servers customization list and a row's More actions menu
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Menu construction reads existing observable definitions and constructs actions synchronously. Configuration discovery and file removal run only when Uninstall is invoked; neither is added to list startup, rendering, scrolling, or menu opening.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected row and a small fixed-size action list per menu invocation, rather than all configured servers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous menu construction; action objects belong to the menu's DisposableStore and are disposed on hide.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: McpServer.readDefinitions returns its existing _fullDefinitions observable. No new cache, file read, or per-row resource-resolution cache miss is introduced during menu construction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced showMcpServerActions, getMcpServerActions, management-action construction, and McpServer.readDefinitions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings measured; changes on this path are bounded action allocations and short action-array scans.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new removal callback is lazy, extra actions are disposed, and output ordering does not execute output or uninstall work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Uninstall a server from an editable shared Copilot CLI configuration or workspace-root .mcp.json
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For Copilot configuration, resolve host configuration resource and read/parse that file before confirmation. After confirmation, await the scanner's serialized read/edit/revalidation/write. Workspace-root configurations use an existing installed-server configuration without discovery or an initial file read. List refresh follows existing file watchers asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve a small host discovery-data object through the main-process or remote-agent NativeMcpDiscoveryHelper channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One RPC for a Copilot candidate per action; zero for a workspace-root match. Browser-local implementation returns undefined without IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These built-in rows had no uninstall action. Existing detail/configuration workflows already used this resolver when the agent host was enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before editable-source confirmation; existing resolver timeout is five seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Desktop helper awaits shell-environment resolution, which can launch a login shell on eligible Unix hosts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one shared shell-resolution attempt per application process, not per removal or server. Zero new launches once the existing promise is populated; Windows and eligible CLI launches skip it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same shell resolution was already used by startup and native MCP discovery and cached process-wide.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only cold/in-flight desktop discovery waits for the shared promise; this does not add a shell process for each action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read selected shared configuration; on confirmed removal edit its JSON, re-read to detect concurrent modifications, and write with etag/mtime protection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For an existing, successfully modified Copilot file: three reads total and one write. For a workspace-root match: two reads and one write. Cancellation after Copilot confirmation preparation performs only its initial read. Existing watchers subsequently read once per coalesced affected-resource update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No removal path existed for these built-in rows. The scanner and its conflict-checking I/O were already used for shared-file editing and other uninstall workflows; watcher placement and coalescing are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preparation read precedes confirmation; modification reads/write precede action completion; watcher refresh is subsequent asynchronous work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One server name and one configuration resource per explicit action. JSON work scales with that file's bytes/server count. Refresh reads are grouped per affected resource/watcher, not per row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery then confirmation then modification are sequential within the action. Scanner modifications are queued by canonical URI, with independent files allowed concurrently. Existing native/workspace discovery watchers debounce changes by 500ms; applicable management watchers use 50ms. No new bulk scheduling or concurrency burst is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workspace-root lookup uses existing _local entries. Copilot resource resolution has no result cache and performs one discovery RPC per action on desktop or remote. Desktop shell-environment resolution uses the existing process-wide cached promise, including in-flight work; it does not spawn per server. Each confirmed modification re-reads the file for conflict detection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced callbacks into removeMcpServers and withSharedMcpServersFile, canonical-URI queue ownership, discovery helper implementation, shell promise caching, and existing watcher schedulers.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: File sizes and I/O latency are unmeasured. Large files make parsing more costly, but this remains one explicit single-file mutation rather than collection-wide fan-out.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. New I/O implements the requested explicit removal; resource-level serialization, conflict checks, and existing refresh coalescing are retained.

Scenarios.Scenario: Invoke Uninstall for an unsupported external configuration or extension-provided server, then optionally reveal its source
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Origin-backed rows resolve whether the source is editable before showing the explanatory dialog. Extension-only rows skip configuration resolution. Opening configuration or extension details occurs only after a separate user choice in the dialog.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Obtain host discovery metadata to compare the supported Copilot configuration URI with the selected origin.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one discovery RPC per origin-backed invocation, including warm/unsupported cases; zero for an extension-only row. No selected-file read after an unsupported-source mismatch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These rows had no Uninstall action. Show Configuration/Show Extension already existed separately and did not require this new explanatory action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes the explanatory dialog and is subject to the resolver's existing five-second timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the selected configuration resource in the existing editor path, which resolves its contents as needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resource opening per explicit Show Configuration selection; an already-open model may avoid fresh file I/O.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same source action was already available and opened the same single configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only affects the separately requested source-editor opening, not menu construction or automatic removal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fallback to getExtensions for one extension identifier if it is absent from installed extensions before opening its detail editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero fallback lookups for an installed contributing extension; one targeted logical lookup for a missing extension, only after explicit Show Extension.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing Show Extension used the identical open method and installed-first fallback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of optional extension-detail opening after the explanatory dialog.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected origin or extension per invocation. Extension-name lookup scans installed extensions once; source opening handles one resource/extension.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One asynchronous action with sequential discovery/dialog handling. No loops across servers and no automatic retries; source opening is explicitly requested.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unsupported origins do not trigger a configuration-file read after URI mismatch, though discovery has one RPC and no negative-result cache. Extension opening prefers the installed extension; only an absent extension requires a gallery lookup. Existing editor/model caches apply to source-file opening.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced unsupported URI exit, extension-only bypass, dialog result gating, ShowConfiguration, and installed-first ExtensionsWorkbenchService.open.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote round-trip and source-editor latency are not measured. Unsupported-source resolution adds one bounded RPC to a new user-requested action, not per row or render.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. The new action has bounded discovery overhead, and potentially expensive source opening remains explicitly user-gated; no collection fan-out or repeated background work is added.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or refresh the MCP server detail form with the agent host disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing renderItem launches asynchronous editable-source resolution while rendering source/definition presentation immediately. The changed option permits disabled-host Copilot configuration resolution; the editable form appears after resource resolution and file parsing. Existing definition loading remains independent. Saving still requires an explicit Save click.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve Copilot configuration host data even while agent-host enablement is false.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One discovery RPC per non-workspace-root detail resolution on desktop/remote. Workspace-root matches avoid it; no per-list-row calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Disabled-host resolution returned undefined before discovery; enabled-host detail resolution already issued the same RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delays editable-form availability but not initial detail presentation or the independently loaded read-only definition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/parse the matching Copilot configuration for a form; independently load a source definition if needed; persist explicit form edits through existing shared-file scanner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new form-resolution read for a matching disabled-host Copilot source per resolution. The pre-existing definition path may independently read one source file when config metadata is absent. Saving a changed shared file uses the existing two-read/one-write conflict-checked mutation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Disabled-host Copilot details lacked the editable form and its read/save path; read-only definition loading already existed. Enabled-host form loading and save I/O are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Form read gates editable-form availability; definition loading is independent; mutation gates only the explicit save.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One displayed detail server per input/presentation refresh. File parsing scales with the selected Copilot configuration's bytes; form controls scale with that server's settings. This is not an eager form for every list row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Form resolution is asynchronous and can overlap independent read-only-definition loading. Existing render generation controls result application rather than cancelling I/O. Save has an existing saving guard, and scanner writes serialize per canonical resource. None of these scheduling rules are changed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workspace-root matches use existing installed state. Copilot resolution has no new cache; desktop shell work is process-wide coalesced. The form is created once on first editable input and reused, and setInput skips reset for unchanged configuration or during saving. Render-generation checks prevent obsolete results from changing the form.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced renderItem and generation-checked resolveSourceFormInput, independent loadSourceDefinition, lazy form allocation, setInput reuse, Save guarding, and shared-file scanner serialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured detail-load times or refresh frequencies. Additional work is for the one visible editable configuration and intended support while the host is disabled.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This enables editing on a previously unsupported state without moving discovery onto list startup, constructing forms per row, or changing existing refresh multiplicity.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all eight changed files and every diff page against base 152c494bd80902ecb06cd1c8e7997ee9455e8b77. Traced menu/action lifetime, explicit shared-file removal, unsupported-source explanation, disabled-host detail editing, IPC discovery, shared shell caching, file mutation serialization, and watcher coalescing. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance bugs or concrete performance-regression fixes qualified for submission. Static review only; magnitudes are unmeasured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
